title: Blob Storage and CDNs
summary: Keep large files out of the database and move them close to readers.
keyPoints: Object stores hold immutable bytes while the database holds small, queryable metadata.
Presigned URLs let clients upload and download directly, so application servers never carry the bytes.
Multipart uploads make large transfers resumable, parallel, and verifiable with checksums.
Versioning, lifecycle rules, and encryption protect durability, recovery, and cost.
A CDN caches public objects at the edge; private objects need signed URLs and careful cache keys.
Versioned object keys are safer than purge calls when content changes.

complexity.note: No bytes pass through the API server.
Throughput depends on the client link and part size.
The origin is skipped on a hit.
Each part can be retried independently.

commonMistakes: Storing image or video bytes as large blobs in the primary database.
Routing every upload and download through application servers instead of using direct storage access.
Making private objects public because signed URLs add a step.
Assuming a CDN purge is instant and global, then serving stale content after an in-place replace.
interviewNotes: Separate the metadata path from the bytes path, and say which store is authoritative for each.
Walk through the upload as sign, direct write, commit, verify, then enqueue follow-up work.
Name multipart upload and checksums when files can be large or connections unreliable.
For private content, use short-lived signed URLs and explain why a shared edge key is unsafe.
Cover durability, versioning, lifecycle, encryption, and the cost of storage and egress.

checkYourself.question: Why keep large files out of a relational database?
checkYourself.answer: Large values inflate backups, replication, logs, and memory use, and they make row queries slower. An object store is built for large immutable bytes.

checkYourself.question: What does a presigned URL authorize?
checkYourself.answer: It carries a signature that permits one operation, such as PUT or GET, on one object key for a limited time, often with constraints on content type and size.

checkYourself.question: Why version the object key instead of purging the CDN?
checkYourself.answer: A new key cannot serve old bytes, while a purge is best effort and may take time to reach every edge location.
